source_text: Omnis sacerdos inter homines parvus ad illum: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Magnus sacerdos Christus.
thought_title: Every priest is small; Christ is the great priest
orientation: Origen is contrasting the Levitical priests, who are small among men, with Christ, who is the great priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
pass_a_gloss: Every priest among men [is] small [compared] to him: You are [a] priest into eternity according to [the] order [of] Melchisedech. [A] great priest [is] Christ.

choices.why: Keeps the spatial/rank metaphor of the Latin, contrasting with 'magnus' (great) applied to Christ.
Preserves the prepositional phrase showing the sphere in which the priest is small.
Renders the comparative force of 'ad' with the accusative, showing the standard of comparison is Christ.
Standard rendering of the temporal phrase, preserving the eternal duration of Christ's priesthood.

choices.english: according to the order of Melchizedek
choices.why: Keeps the technical phrase from Psalm 110:4, preserving the proper name and the word 'order'.
Preserves the noun 'sacerdos' as 'priest' per glossary and the adjective 'magnus' as 'great', contrasting with 'parvus'.

bible_refs.note: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech

pass_b_english: Every priest among men is small in comparison to him: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Psalm 110:4). Christ is the great priest.

last_rejected.source_quote: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech
last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 109:4, not Hebrew Psalm 110:4; LXX numbering differs.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin source lacks any scripture reference; 'Psalm 110:4' is translator's helpful addition, not a mistranslation of source words.
